* fix(cache): stop unindexable untracked files disabling the search cache

worktreeSnapshotCacheable required a wholly pristine working tree before it
would reuse a tree-keyed index. It asked WorktreeMatchesHEAD, which is a plain
`git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` compared against empty output, so
a single file no parser ever opens — .DS_Store, a compiled binary, a log, an
editor swap file — disabled the cache for the entire repository and every query
re-indexed from scratch.

Measured on this repo before the change: index_cache_hit=false and
index_latency_ms=9062 on a back-to-back repeat of the same search.

A path that cannot contribute a symbol or a relation cannot make a snapshot
stale, so it is not a reason to discard one. The gate now forgives exactly those
paths and nothing else:

  - gitutil gains WorktreeDirtyPaths, the factual list of diverging paths.
    WorktreeMatchesHEAD becomes len(paths)==0 and keeps its contract, so its
    existing callers and tests are unaffected. Both sides of a rename are
    reported, since porcelain -z spends a second record on the source path.
  - worktreeSnapshotCacheable forgives a dirty path only when
    extensionUnsupported says so — the same predicate the indexer uses to skip a
    file, so the two cannot disagree about what is read.

Conservative in the safe direction. An extensionless path counts as supported,
because a shebang can make it a script. Any supported path still bypasses the
cache whatever its status, and the forgiveness is per-path rather than a blanket
"ignore untracked". A .gitignore edit is forgiven, which is sound: ignore rules
can only change whether UNTRACKED files are walked, and an untracked file that
is indexable already fails the gate on its own.

Tests: WorktreeDirtyPaths over clean/untracked/modified/renamed/ignored trees,
and a snapshot-level pair asserting an unindexable untracked file keeps the cache
warm with an identical symbol set while an untracked .go file, and an
extensionless file, both still bypass it.

* fix(cache): do not forgive manifests the resolver reads, and unpin the test from the developer's global gitignore

Two problems with forgiving unindexable dirty paths, plus the comment that led to
the first.

extensionUnsupported decides whether a file is PARSED, but parsing is not the only
way a file reaches the graph. buildManifestImportResolver also reads the CONTENT of
the repo-root manifests, and two of those — go.mod and setup.cfg — carry no
supported extension while deciding how every import in the repository resolves.
Editing go.mod alone therefore kept the cache warm and served call edges still
resolved against the previous module path:

    module example.com/old -> example.com/renamed, go.mod the only dirty file
    before: Index: cache-hit   Callers: - main (main.go:5) [import_resolved]
    after:  Index: cache-miss  Callers: - none

They are now excluded by name through isManifestImportFile, listed beside the
resolver in manifestImportFiles. TestManifestImportFilesCoverReads walks
buildManifestImportResolver's AST for readContent string literals and fails if the
list falls behind, so the two cannot drift — the guarantee the doc comment claimed
but did not have. The win this change exists for is unaffected: a stray .DS_Store,
.log or .o still keeps the cache warm, and an untracked .go still bypasses it.

TestWorktreeDirtyPaths asserted that an untracked .DS_Store is reported, but
newWorktreeRepo left core.excludesFile alone, so git status honoured the
developer's global ignore. The stock macOS one lists .DS_Store — GitHub's own
gitignore guidance recommends it — making the case green on CI runners, which have
no global ignore, and red on the machine of anyone who followed that advice. The
fixture now points core.excludesFile at an empty file outside the repo, which makes
all five subtests hermetic rather than just this one.

The doc comment on worktreeSnapshotCacheable claimed extensionUnsupported was "the
same predicate the indexer uses to skip a file, so the two can never disagree about
what is read". Rewritten to say what is true, including the ignore-rule asymmetry:
git never ignores a tracked file while the provider's walk applies the ignore stack
to every path, and that disagreement can only ever report a path as dirty that the
walk would have skipped — costing a re-index, never serving a stale snapshot.

filed EVERY unrecognized token under paths. A mistyped flag therefore became a path
filter that matches nothing:

    $ entire graph diff --base HEAD~1 --head HEAD --jsonn
    Semantic changes HEAD~1..HEAD

    No semantic entity changes detected.
    $ echo $?

typo. Now:

    $ entire graph diff --base HEAD~1 --head HEAD --jsonn
    diff does not accept --jsonn in entire-graph dev: this binary may be older than
    the caller that built the command line; run "entire graph diff --help" for the
    flags it does accept (unexpected: --jsonn)
    $ echo $?

Extracted parseDiffFlags, which returns flag-shaped unknowns separately from path
filters so runDiff can reject them through the same unexpectedArgumentsError every
other verb uses. Paths that genuinely look like flags keep working: parseDiffFlags
splits on `--` itself rather than letting parseCommonFlags flatten the separator
away, so `diff -- --base` still means the path named `--base`. Bare positional
paths are unchanged.

`git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` compared against empty output, so
a single file no parser ever opens — .DS_Store, a compiled binary, a log, an
editor swap file — disabled the cache for the entire repository and every query
re-indexed from scratch.

Measured on this repo before the change: index_cache_hit=false and
index_latency_ms=9062 on a back-to-back repeat of the same search.

A path that cannot contribute a symbol or a relation cannot make a snapshot
stale, so it is not a reason to discard one. The gate now forgives exactly those
paths and nothing else:

  - gitutil gains WorktreeDirtyPaths, the factual list of diverging paths.
    WorktreeMatchesHEAD becomes len(paths)==0 and keeps its contract, so its
    existing callers and tests are unaffected. Both sides of a rename are
    reported, since porcelain -z spends a second record on the source path.
  - worktreeSnapshotCacheable forgives a dirty path only when
    extensionUnsupported says so — the same predicate the indexer uses to skip a
    file, so the two cannot disagree about what is read.

Conservative in the safe direction. An extensionless path counts as supported,
because a shebang can make it a script. Any supported path still bypasses the
cache whatever its status, and the forgiveness is per-path rather than a blanket
"ignore untracked". A .gitignore edit is forgiven, which is sound: ignore rules
can only change whether UNTRACKED files are walked, and an untracked file that
is indexable already fails the gate on its own.

Tests: WorktreeDirtyPaths over clean/untracked/modified/renamed/ignored trees,
and a snapshot-level pair asserting an unindexable untracked file keeps the cache
warm with an identical symbol set while an untracked .go file, and an
extensionless file, both still bypass it.

* fix(cache): do not forgive manifests the resolver reads, and unpin the test from the developer's global gitignore

the first.

extensionUnsupported decides whether a file is PARSED, but parsing is not the only
way a file reaches the graph. buildManifestImportResolver also reads the CONTENT of
the repo-root manifests, and two of those — go.mod and setup.cfg — carry no
supported extension while deciding how every import in the repository resolves.
Editing go.mod alone therefore kept the cache warm and served call edges still
resolved against the previous module path:

    module example.com/old -> example.com/renamed, go.mod the only dirty file
    before: Index: cache-hit   Callers: - main (main.go:5) [import_resolved]
    after:  Index: cache-miss  Callers: - none

resolver in manifestImportFiles. TestManifestImportFilesCoverReads walks
buildManifestImportResolver's AST for readContent string literals and fails if the
list falls behind, so the two cannot drift — the guarantee the doc comment claimed
but did not have. The win this change exists for is unaffected: a stray .DS_Store,
.log or .o still keeps the cache warm, and an untracked .go still bypasses it.

newWorktreeRepo left core.excludesFile alone, so git status honoured the
developer's global ignore. The stock macOS one lists .DS_Store — GitHub's own

no global ignore, and red on the machine of anyone who followed that advice. The
fixture now points core.excludesFile at an empty file outside the repo, which makes
all five subtests hermetic rather than just this one.

what is read". Rewritten to say what is true, including the ignore-rule asymmetry:

- Subscription: enabled AzureCloud subscription, `Entire Pay As You Go`.

Run Command does not need RDP, WinRM, SSH, or another inbound rule. Output is limited to the last 4,096 bytes and execution to 90 minutes. [Azure Windows Run Command](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/windows/run-command), [Azure CLI syntax](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cli/azure/vm/run-command?view=azure-cli-latest).

For reliable Scoop/GitHub egress, the simplest test VM has a Standard public IP but **no inbound NSG rule**. A private-only VM also works with Run Command, but needs NAT Gateway or another explicit outbound path.

## Proposed Azure commands

Use a fresh resource group; do not reuse an existing workload group.

```sh
EG_RUN="$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)"
EG_LOCATION="westus3"
EG_RESOURCE_GROUP="rg-entire-graph-win-smoke-${EG_RUN}"
EG_VM="eg-win-smoke"
EG_NSG="nsg-eg-win-smoke"
EG_PUBLIC_IP="pip-eg-win-smoke"
EG_SIZE="Standard_B2s"

test "$(az group exists --name "$EG_RESOURCE_GROUP")" = "false" || {
  echo "Resource group already exists; stop."
  return 1
}

az group create \
  --name "$EG_RESOURCE_GROUP" \
  --location "$EG_LOCATION" \
  --tags purpose=entire-graph-windows-smoke ttl=24h
```

Supply the temporary password through a hidden prompt rather than putting it in shell history:

```sh
read -s "EG_VM_ADMIN_PASSWORD?Temporary Windows admin password: "
echo

az vm create \
  --resource-group "$EG_RESOURCE_GROUP" \
  --name "$EG_VM" \
  --location "$EG_LOCATION" \
  --image Win2022AzureEditionCore \
  --size "$EG_SIZE" \
  --admin-username egadmin \
  --authentication-type password \
  --admin-password "$EG_VM_ADMIN_PASSWORD" \
  --storage-sku StandardSSD_LRS \
  --nsg "$EG_NSG" \
  --nsg-rule NONE \
  --public-ip-address "$EG_PUBLIC_IP" \
  --public-ip-sku Standard \
  --os-disk-delete-option Delete \
  --nic-delete-option Delete \
  --tags purpose=entire-graph-windows-smoke ttl=24h \
  --query '{id:id,provisioningState:provisioningState,privateIp:privateIps,publicIp:publicIpAddress}' \
  --output json

unset EG_VM_ADMIN_PASSWORD
```

Verify the agent and absence of custom inbound rules:

```sh
az vm get-instance-view \
  --resource-group "$EG_RESOURCE_GROUP" \
  --name "$EG_VM" \
  --query '{power:instanceView.statuses[1].displayStatus,agent:instanceView.vmAgent.statuses[0].displayStatus}' \
  --output json

az network nsg rule list \
  --resource-group "$EG_RESOURCE_GROUP" \
  --nsg-name "$EG_NSG" \
  --output table

az vm run-command show \
  --location "$EG_LOCATION" \
  --command-id RunPowerShellScript \
  --query '{id:id,label:label,osType:osType}' \
  --output json
```

The custom NSG-rule list should be empty.

## PowerShell smoke script

Save locally as `windows-smoke.ps1`. Run Command executes as SYSTEM, so Scoop’s documented administrator override is necessary. The actual Entire installation commands remain the current official Windows commands. [Entire installation](https://docs.entire.io/installation), [Scoop administrator installation](https://github.com/ScoopInstaller/Install/blob/master/README.md).

```powershell
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
[Net.ServicePointManager]::SecurityProtocol = [Net.SecurityProtocolType]::Tls12
Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope Process -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Force

function Assert-NativeSuccess([string] $Step) {
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
        throw "$Step failed with exit code $LASTEXITCODE"
    }
}

$root = 'C:\eg-smoke'
$scoopDir = Join-Path $root 'scoop'
$scoopGlobalDir = Join-Path $root 'scoop-global'
$installer = Join-Path $root 'install-scoop.ps1'
$fixture = Join-Path $root 'fixture'

New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $root -Force | Out-Null
if (Test-Path $fixture) {
    throw "Fixture already exists: $fixture"
}

Invoke-WebRequest -UseBasicParsing -Uri 'https://get.scoop.sh' -OutFile $installer
& $installer -RunAsAdmin -ScoopDir $scoopDir -ScoopGlobalDir $scoopGlobalDir
Assert-NativeSuccess 'Scoop installation'

$env:SCOOP = $scoopDir
$env:SCOOP_GLOBAL = $scoopGlobalDir
$env:Path = "$scoopDir\shims;$env:Path"

scoop install git
Assert-NativeSuccess 'Git installation'

scoop bucket add entire https://github.com/entireio/scoop-bucket.git
Assert-NativeSuccess 'Entire bucket addition'

scoop install entire/cli
Assert-NativeSuccess 'Entire CLI installation'

$entireVersion = (& entire version 2>&1 | Out-String).Trim()
Assert-NativeSuccess 'Entire version'

$pluginInstall = (& entire plugin install graph 2>&1 | Out-String).Trim()
Assert-NativeSuccess 'Entire Graph plugin installation'

$graphVersion = (& entire graph version 2>&1 | Out-String).Trim()
Assert-NativeSuccess 'Entire Graph version'

New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $fixture | Out-Null
Set-Location $fixture

$source = @'
package fixture

func Greet() string {
	return "hello"
}

func MainFlow() string {
	return Greet()
}
'@

[IO.File]::WriteAllText(
    (Join-Path $fixture 'fixture.go'),
    $source,
    (New-Object Text.UTF8Encoding($false))
)

git init
Assert-NativeSuccess 'git init'
git config user.name 'Entire Graph Windows Smoke'
git config user.email 'windows-smoke@example.invalid'
git add fixture.go
git commit -m 'Add smoke fixture'
Assert-NativeSuccess 'fixture commit'

$activation = (& entire graph init-agents --repo $fixture 2>&1 | Out-String).Trim()
Assert-NativeSuccess 'init-agents'

$expected = @(
    (Join-Path $fixture '.entire\graph-agent.md'),
    (Join-Path $fixture 'AGENTS.md'),
    (Join-Path $fixture 'CLAUDE.md')
)
foreach ($path in $expected) {
    if (-not (Test-Path $path -PathType Leaf)) {
        throw "Expected activation file missing: $path"
    }
}

git add .entire AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md
git commit -m 'Activate Entire Graph'
Assert-NativeSuccess 'activation commit'

$search = (& entire graph search `
    --repo $fixture `
    --query 'find where the greeting is implemented and what calls it' `
    --format agent `
    --top-k 3 `
    --max-context-bytes 2500 2>&1 | Out-String).Trim()
Assert-NativeSuccess 'graph search'

Write-Output '=== Entire version ==='
Write-Output $entireVersion
Write-Output '=== Graph version ==='
Write-Output $graphVersion
Write-Output '=== Plugin installation ==='
Write-Output $pluginInstall
Write-Output '=== Activation ==='
Write-Output $activation
Write-Output '=== Git status ==='
git status --short
Write-Output '=== Search ==='
Write-Output $search
```

Invoke it:

```sh
az vm run-command invoke \
  --resource-group "$EG_RESOURCE_GROUP" \
  --name "$EG_VM" \
  --command-id RunPowerShellScript \
  --scripts @windows-smoke.ps1 \
  --query 'value[].message' \
  --output tsv
```

Inspect the exact isolated group first:

az resource list \
  --resource-group "$EG_RESOURCE_GROUP" \
  --query '[].{name:name,type:type,location:location}' \

Then require an exact-name confirmation:

```sh
read "EG_DELETE_CONFIRM?Type the resource-group name to delete: "

  echo "Name mismatch; not deleting."
  return 1
}

az group delete \
  --name "$EG_RESOURCE_GROUP" \
  --yes \
  --no-wait

az group wait \
  --name "$EG_RESOURCE_GROUP" \
  --deleted
```

## Recommendation

- Subscription: enabled AzureCloud subscription, `Entire Pay As You Go`.
- Region: `westus3`, matching the existing workload footprint.
- Quota: 65 free regional vCPUs and 65 free BS-family vCPUs.
- Image: `Win2022AzureEditionCore` — confirmed x64, Hyper-V V2. `Win2022Datacenter` is also x64/V2.
- Size: `Standard_B2s` (2 vCPU, 4 GiB); fallback `Standard_B2ms` (2 vCPU, 8 GiB), then `Standard_D2s_v5`.
- SKU metadata is present, but `az vm list-skus` unexpectedly returned no restriction rows; final allocation availability is therefore not proven until creation.

Run Command does not need RDP, WinRM, SSH, or another inbound rule. It uses the Azure VM Agent, runs Windows scripts as SYSTEM, and requires outbound TCP 443 plus `Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/runCommand/action`. Output is limited to the last 4,096 bytes and execution to 90 minutes. [Azure Windows Run Command](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/windows/run-command), [Azure CLI syntax](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cli/azure/vm/run-command?view=azure-cli-latest).

For reliable Scoop/GitHub egress, the simplest test VM has a Standard public IP but **no inbound NSG rule**. A private-only VM also works with Run Command, but needs NAT Gateway or another explicit outbound path.

## Proposed Azure commands

Use a fresh resource group; do not reuse an existing workload group.

```sh
EG_RUN="$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)"
EG_LOCATION="westus3"
EG_RESOURCE_GROUP="rg-entire-graph-win-smoke-${EG_RUN}"
EG_VM="eg-win-smoke"
EG_NSG="nsg-eg-win-smoke"
EG_PUBLIC_IP="pip-eg-win-smoke"
EG_SIZE="Standard_B2s"

test "$(az group exists --name "$EG_RESOURCE_GROUP")" = "false" || {
  echo "Resource group already exists; stop."
  return 1
}

az group create \
  --name "$EG_RESOURCE_GROUP" \
  --location "$EG_LOCATION" \
  --tags purpose=entire-graph-windows-smoke ttl=24h
```

Supply the temporary password through a hidden prompt rather than putting it in shell history:

```sh
read -s "EG_VM_ADMIN_PASSWORD?Temporary Windows admin password: "
echo

az vm create \
  --resource-group "$EG_RESOURCE_GROUP" \
  --name "$EG_VM" \
  --location "$EG_LOCATION" \
  --image Win2022AzureEditionCore \
  --size "$EG_SIZE" \
  --admin-username egadmin \
  --authentication-type password \
  --admin-password "$EG_VM_ADMIN_PASSWORD" \
  --storage-sku StandardSSD_LRS \
  --nsg "$EG_NSG" \
  --nsg-rule NONE \
  --public-ip-address "$EG_PUBLIC_IP" \
  --public-ip-sku Standard \
  --os-disk-delete-option Delete \
  --nic-delete-option Delete \
  --tags purpose=entire-graph-windows-smoke ttl=24h \
  --query '{id:id,provisioningState:provisioningState,privateIp:privateIps,publicIp:publicIpAddress}' \
  --output json

unset EG_VM_ADMIN_PASSWORD
```

Verify the agent and absence of custom inbound rules:

```sh
az vm get-instance-view \
  --resource-group "$EG_RESOURCE_GROUP" \
  --name "$EG_VM" \
  --query '{power:instanceView.statuses[1].displayStatus,agent:instanceView.vmAgent.statuses[0].displayStatus}' \
  --output json

az network nsg rule list \
  --resource-group "$EG_RESOURCE_GROUP" \
  --nsg-name "$EG_NSG" \
  --output table

az vm run-command show \
  --location "$EG_LOCATION" \
  --command-id RunPowerShellScript \
  --query '{id:id,label:label,osType:osType}' \
  --output json
```

The custom NSG-rule list should be empty.

## PowerShell smoke script

Save locally as `windows-smoke.ps1`. Run Command executes as SYSTEM, so Scoop’s documented administrator override is necessary. The actual Entire installation commands remain the current official Windows commands. [Entire installation](https://docs.entire.io/installation), [Scoop administrator installation](https://github.com/ScoopInstaller/Install/blob/master/README.md).

```powershell
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
[Net.ServicePointManager]::SecurityProtocol = [Net.SecurityProtocolType]::Tls12
Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope Process -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Force

function Assert-NativeSuccess([string] $Step) {
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
        throw "$Step failed with exit code $LASTEXITCODE"
    }
}

$root = 'C:\eg-smoke'
$scoopDir = Join-Path $root 'scoop'
$scoopGlobalDir = Join-Path $root 'scoop-global'
$installer = Join-Path $root 'install-scoop.ps1'
$fixture = Join-Path $root 'fixture'

New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $root -Force | Out-Null
if (Test-Path $fixture) {
    throw "Fixture already exists: $fixture"
}

Invoke-WebRequest -UseBasicParsing -Uri 'https://get.scoop.sh' -OutFile $installer
& $installer -RunAsAdmin -ScoopDir $scoopDir -ScoopGlobalDir $scoopGlobalDir
Assert-NativeSuccess 'Scoop installation'

$env:SCOOP = $scoopDir
$env:SCOOP_GLOBAL = $scoopGlobalDir
$env:Path = "$scoopDir\shims;$env:Path"

scoop install git
Assert-NativeSuccess 'Git installation'

scoop bucket add entire https://github.com/entireio/scoop-bucket.git
Assert-NativeSuccess 'Entire bucket addition'

scoop install entire/cli
Assert-NativeSuccess 'Entire CLI installation'

$entireVersion = (& entire version 2>&1 | Out-String).Trim()
Assert-NativeSuccess 'Entire version'

$pluginInstall = (& entire plugin install graph 2>&1 | Out-String).Trim()
Assert-NativeSuccess 'Entire Graph plugin installation'

$graphVersion = (& entire graph version 2>&1 | Out-String).Trim()
Assert-NativeSuccess 'Entire Graph version'

New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $fixture | Out-Null
Set-Location $fixture

$source = @'
package fixture

func Greet() string {
	return "hello"
}

func MainFlow() string {
	return Greet()
}
'@

[IO.File]::WriteAllText(
    (Join-Path $fixture 'fixture.go'),
    $source,
    (New-Object Text.UTF8Encoding($false))
)

git init
Assert-NativeSuccess 'git init'
git config user.name 'Entire Graph Windows Smoke'
git config user.email 'windows-smoke@example.invalid'
git add fixture.go
git commit -m 'Add smoke fixture'
Assert-NativeSuccess 'fixture commit'

$activation = (& entire graph init-agents --repo $fixture 2>&1 | Out-String).Trim()
Assert-NativeSuccess 'init-agents'

$expected = @(
    (Join-Path $fixture '.entire\graph-agent.md'),
    (Join-Path $fixture 'AGENTS.md'),
    (Join-Path $fixture 'CLAUDE.md')
)
foreach ($path in $expected) {
    if (-not (Test-Path $path -PathType Leaf)) {
        throw "Expected activation file missing: $path"
    }
}

git add .entire AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md
git commit -m 'Activate Entire Graph'
Assert-NativeSuccess 'activation commit'

$search = (& entire graph search `
    --repo $fixture `
    --query 'find where the greeting is implemented and what calls it' `
    --format agent `
    --top-k 3 `
    --max-context-bytes 2500 2>&1 | Out-String).Trim()
Assert-NativeSuccess 'graph search'

Write-Output '=== Entire version ==='
Write-Output $entireVersion
Write-Output '=== Graph version ==='
Write-Output $graphVersion
Write-Output '=== Plugin installation ==='
Write-Output $pluginInstall
Write-Output '=== Activation ==='
Write-Output $activation
Write-Output '=== Git status ==='
git status --short
Write-Output '=== Search ==='
Write-Output $search
```

Invoke it:

```sh
az vm run-command invoke \
  --resource-group "$EG_RESOURCE_GROUP" \
  --name "$EG_VM" \
  --command-id RunPowerShellScript \
  --scripts @windows-smoke.ps1 \
  --query 'value[].message' \
  --output tsv
```

## Teardown

Inspect the exact isolated group first:

```sh
az group show \
  --name "$EG_RESOURCE_GROUP" \
  --query '{name:name,location:location,tags:tags}' \
  --output json

az resource list \
  --resource-group "$EG_RESOURCE_GROUP" \
  --query '[].{name:name,type:type,location:location}' \
  --output table
```

Then require an exact-name confirmation:

```sh
read "EG_DELETE_CONFIRM?Type the resource-group name to delete: "
test "$EG_DELETE_CONFIRM" = "$EG_RESOURCE_GROUP" || {
  echo "Name mismatch; not deleting."
  return 1
}

az group delete \
  --name "$EG_RESOURCE_GROUP" \
  --yes \
  --no-wait

az group wait \
  --name "$EG_RESOURCE_GROUP" \
  --deleted
```

Message Type: FINAL_ANSWER
Task name: /root
Sender: /root/windows_surface
Payload:
Windows CI surface and cause:

- Workflow: `.github/workflows/test.yml`
  - `windows-latest`
  - `actions/checkout@v6`
  - `actions/setup-go@v6`, `go-version: "1.26.x"`
  - Exact command: `go test ./...`
- Failing runner:
  - Windows Server 2025, build `10.0.26100`
  - Image `windows-2025-vs2026`, version `20260818.207.1`
  - Go `1.26.6 windows/amd64`
  - PowerShell 7, `GOTOOLCHAIN=local`
- Focused reproduction:
  - `go test ./internal/sem -run '^TestGitMetadataGuardAllowsSubstSubdirectoryRepository$' -count=1 -v`

The only failure is `TestGitMetadataGuardAllowsSubstSubdirectoryRepository` at `provider_gitdir_unc_windows_test.go:1003`.

Root cause: the PR’s physical-path resolver handoff happens after an earlier bare-repository probe. For a repository entered through `SUBST`:

1. The resolver starts anchored to the alias, e.g. `Z:\`.
2. `resolver.lstat(dir\HEAD)` opens the parent and canonicalizes it to the backing path, e.g. `C:\...\checkout\subdir`.
3. `lstat` then compares that physical `C:` path against its original `Z:` anchor and returns `errSymlinkChainOffVolume`.
4. `bareGitMetadataDirectorySafeWithResolver` reports `safe=false`.
5. `gitMetadataSafeForSubprocess` returns false before reaching the newly added block that would switch to a physical resolver.

The analogous junction test passes because junction aliases remain on the same drive volume. This is a deterministic resolver-ordering/namespace bug introduced with commit `321af0`, not a flaky test fixture. No files were edited.

Message Type: FINAL_ANSWER
Task name: /root
Sender: /root/pr_ci
Payload:
PR 132 CI findings:

- Head: `security/git-dir-always-excluded` at `321af0fb07678c3ca5d1e7ce4be3c9fa438e3084`
- Workflow run: [32614255197](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/actions/runs/32614255197)
- Failing job: `test (windows-latest)`, [job 97137287851](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/actions/runs/32614255197/job/97137287851)
- CI command: `go test ./...` using Go 1.26.6
- Sole failing test:

```text
--- FAIL: TestGitMetadataGuardAllowsSubstSubdirectoryRepository
    provider_gitdir_unc_windows_test.go:1003:
    safe repository discovered from a SUBST subdirectory was refused
FAIL github.com/entireio/entire-graph/internal/sem
```

The failure is a false rejection of a safe Windows `SUBST` path. The test aliases a physical temp directory, typically on `D:`, as `Z:` and runs discovery from `Z:\checkout\subdir`. The resolver canonicalizes the opened parent back to its physical `D:` path, but `sameVolumePathResolver.lstat` then checks it against the lexical `Z:` anchor. `sameVolume` compares drive letters, so it returns off-volume. This occurs during the bare-repository ancestor probe before the newly added physical-resolver switch can run.

Relevant files:

- `internal/sem/provider_gitdir_unc_windows_test.go` — adds the failing SUBST regression.
- `internal/sem/provider.go` — contains `sameVolume`, resolver `lstat`, and the new ancestor-discovery logic.
- `internal/sem/path_volume_windows.go` — canonicalizes handles to physical Windows paths.
- `internal/sem/provider_path_volume_unix_test.go` — analogous Unix coverage, which passes.

The parent commit `5ed477b5602b53e2c789a19a282eab6eb5b4ffc4` had a green run, confirming the latest commit introduced the failure. Windows build itself passes; only the test job fails. No files or external state were changed.

The concrete route is an ephemeral Azure Windows Server 2025 VM in `eastus`, matching CI’s OS, architecture, and region. Azure has sufficient `Standard_D4s_v5` quota. Reproduce synthetic merge commit `3f3dc249785829e22a7e14be71e4eb9936103b7e` with Go 1.26.6 and MinGW/GCC 15.2.0:

```zsh
AZ_PR132_RG=pr132-windows-repro

az group create -n "$AZ_PR132_RG" -l eastus

  -n "$AZ_PR132_VM" \
  -l eastus \
  --image MicrosoftWindowsServer:WindowsServer:2025-datacenter-azure-edition:latest \
  --size Standard_D4s_v5 \
  --admin-username codexadmin \
  --admin-password "$AZ_PR132_PASSWORD" \
  --authentication-type password \
  --nsg-rule NONE \
  --public-ip-address pr132-win2025-pip \
  --public-ip-sku Standard \
  --os-disk-delete-option Delete \
  --nic-delete-option Delete
```

Run a PowerShell bootstrap through Azure Run Command:

```powershell
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
Set-ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Scope Process -Force
[Net.ServicePointManager]::SecurityProtocol = [Net.ServicePointManager]::SecurityProtocol -bor 3072
iex ((New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadString('https://community.chocolatey.org/install.ps1'))

choco install golang --version=1.26.6 -y --no-progress
choco install mingw --version=15.2.0 -y --no-progress

$env:Path = [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('Path','Machine') + ';' +
            [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('Path','User')
$env:GOTOOLCHAIN = 'local'
$env:CGO_ENABLED = '1'

New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force C:\src | Out-Null
Invoke-WebRequest `
  'https://codeload.github.com/entireio/entire-graph/zip/3f3dc249785829e22a7e14be71e4eb9936103b7e' `
  -OutFile C:\src\pr132.zip
Expand-Archive C:\src\pr132.zip C:\src -Force

Set-Location C:\src\entire-graph-3f3dc249785829e22a7e14be71e4eb9936103b7e
go version
gcc --version
go test -v ./internal/sem -run '^TestGitMetadataGuardAllowsSubstSubdirectoryRepository$' -count=1
exit $LASTEXITCODE
```

Invoke it with:

```zsh
az vm run-command invoke \
  -g "$AZ_PR132_RG" \
  -n "$AZ_PR132_VM" \
  --command-id RunPowerShellScript \
  --scripts @/path/to/bootstrap.ps1 \
  --query 'value[].message' \
  -o tsv
```

No VM was started or created, and the repository remains clean.

content.text:
Cause found: PR 132 re-anchors Windows `SUBST` paths too late, causing a safe repository to be rejected as off-volume.

On an Azure Windows VM, using CI’s synthetic merge commit `3f3dc249`, Go 1.26.6, and GCC 15.2.0, I reproduced:

```text
=== RUN   TestGitMetadataGuardAllowsSubstSubdirectoryRepository
provider_gitdir_unc_windows_test.go:1003:
    safe repository discovered from a SUBST subdirectory was refused
--- FAIL
TEST_EXIT=1
```

The control flow is:

1. The test aliases a physical directory as `Z:` and starts discovery under `Z:\checkout\subdir`.
2. [`lstat`](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/blob/321af0fb07678c3ca5d1e7ce4be3c9fa438e3084/internal/sem/provider.go#L11820-L11829) opens that directory and Windows canonicalizes it to its physical backing drive.
3. The resolver is still anchored to `Z:`, so comparing the physical path against that anchor returns `errSymlinkChainOffVolume`.
4. [`gitMetadataSafeForSubprocess`](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/blob/321af0fb07678c3ca5d1e7ce4be3c9fa438e3084/internal/sem/provider.go#L13207-L13233) performs the bare-repository probe before switching to a physical resolver. It therefore returns `false` before reaching the new resolver-handoff block.

This is deterministic, not flaky. Junction coverage passes because the alias and target remain on the same drive. The likely minimal fix is moving the physical-resolver handoff before the bare-repository probe.

No code was changed. The dedicated Azure resource group and its VM, disk, NIC, and VNet were permanently deleted and confirmed gone. The failing [Windows CI job is here](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/actions/runs/32614255197/job/97137287851).

*** Add File: /Users/thomi/.codex/worktrees/caa8/entire-graph/.pr132-windows-verify.ps1
+$ErrorActionPreference = "Continue"
+
+$root = "C:\pr132-fix"
+$mergeSHA = "3f3dc249785829e22a7e14be71e4eb9936103b7e"
+$sourceRoot = Join-Path $root "src"
+$repo = Join-Path $sourceRoot "entire-graph-$mergeSHA"
+
+New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $sourceRoot | Out-Null
+if (-not (Test-Path $repo)) {
+    $archive = Join-Path $sourceRoot "pr132.zip"
+    Invoke-WebRequest -UseBasicParsing -Uri "https://codeload.github.com/entireio/entire-graph/zip/$mergeSHA" -OutFile $archive
+    Expand-Archive -Path $archive -DestinationPath $sourceRoot -Force
+}
+
+$env:Path = [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable("Path", "Machine") + ";" + [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable("Path", "User")
+$env:GOTOOLCHAIN = "local"
+$env:CGO_ENABLED = "1"
+$env:GOMODCACHE = Join-Path $root "gomodcache"
+$env:GOCACHE = Join-Path $root "gocache"
+
+Write-Output "=== environment ==="
+& go version
+& gcc --version | Select-Object -First 1
+& git --version
+Write-Output "COMMIT=$mergeSHA"
+
+Set-Location $repo
+$focused = "go test -v ./internal/sem -run ^TestGitMetadataGuardAllowsSubstSubdirectoryRepository$ -count=1"
+
+Write-Output "=== baseline focused test ==="
+$baselineLog = Join-Path $root "baseline.log"
+& cmd.exe /d /c "$focused > `"$baselineLog`" 2>&1"
+$baselineExit = $LASTEXITCODE
+$baselineText = Get-Content -Raw $baselineLog
+Write-Output $baselineText
+Write-Output "BASELINE_EXIT=$baselineExit"
+if ($baselineExit -eq 0 -or $baselineText -notmatch "safe repository discovered from a SUBST subdirectory was refused") {
+    Write-Error "Baseline did not reproduce the expected PR 132 failure"
+    exit 20
+}
+
+$patchText = @'
+diff --git a/internal/sem/provider.go b/internal/sem/provider.go
+index a922116..43ba4da 100644
+--- a/internal/sem/provider.go
++++ b/internal/sem/provider.go
+@@ -13142,7 +13142,23 @@ func gitMetadataSafeForSubprocess(repo string) bool {
+ 		return false
+ 	}
+ 	defer resolver.Close()
+-	resolvedDiscoveryRoot := false
++	// Git probes the physical working directory for both ordinary and bare
++	// metadata before it walks to a parent. Resolve a symlinked, junctioned, or
++	// SUBST repo up front so every discovery check uses one path namespace.
++	repoHandle, resolvedRepo, resolveErr := resolver.open(repoAbs)
++	if resolveErr != nil {
++		return false
++	}
++	_ = repoHandle.Close()
++	if _, sameNamespace := resolver.anchor.components(resolvedRepo); !sameNamespace {
++		physicalResolver, physicalErr := newSameVolumePathResolver(resolvedRepo)
++		if physicalErr != nil {
++			return false
++		}
++		defer physicalResolver.Close()
++		resolver = physicalResolver
++	}
++	repoAbs = resolvedRepo
+ 	for dir := repoAbs; ; {
+ 		dotGit := filepath.Join(dir, ".git")
+ 		opened, resolvedDotGit, openErr := resolver.open(dotGit)
+@@ -13211,27 +13227,6 @@ func gitMetadataSafeForSubprocess(repo string) bool {
+ 		if bare {
+ 			return true
+ 		}
+-		if !resolvedDiscoveryRoot {
+-			// Git discovers ancestors from the physical working directory. Before
+-			// walking to the first parent, resolve a symlinked or junctioned repo so
+-			// the loop follows the same ancestor chain. Root invocations that find
+-			// their own metadata return above without paying for this extra walk.
+-			repoHandle, resolvedRepo, resolveErr := resolver.open(repoAbs)
+-			if resolveErr != nil {
+-				return false
+-			}
+-			_ = repoHandle.Close()
+-			if _, sameNamespace := resolver.anchor.components(resolvedRepo); !sameNamespace {
+-				physicalResolver, physicalErr := newSameVolumePathResolver(resolvedRepo)
+-				if physicalErr != nil {
+-					return false
+-				}
+-				defer physicalResolver.Close()
+-				resolver = physicalResolver
+-			}
+-			dir = resolvedRepo
+-			resolvedDiscoveryRoot = true
+-		}
+ 		parent := filepath.Dir(dir)
+ 		if parent == dir {
+ 			return true
+diff --git a/internal/sem/provider_gitdir_unc_windows_test.go b/internal/sem/provider_gitdir_unc_windows_test.go
+index 561b153..183569e 100644
+--- a/internal/sem/provider_gitdir_unc_windows_test.go
++++ b/internal/sem/provider_gitdir_unc_windows_test.go
+@@ -998,9 +998,13 @@ func TestGitMetadataGuardAllowsSubstSubdirectoryRepository(t *testing.T) {
+ 		}
+ 	}
+ 	writeFile(t, gitDir, "HEAD", "ref: refs/heads/main\n")
+-	alias := filepath.Join(drive+`\`, "checkout", "subdir")
+-	if !gitMetadataSafeForSubprocess(alias) {
+-		t.Fatal("safe repository discovered from a SUBST subdirectory was refused")
++	for _, alias := range []string{
++		filepath.Join(drive+`\`, "checkout"),
++		filepath.Join(drive+`\`, "checkout", "subdir"),
++	} {
++		if !gitMetadataSafeForSubprocess(alias) {
++			t.Errorf("safe repository discovered from SUBST path %q was refused", alias)
++		}
+ 	}
+ }
+ 
+'@
+$patchPath = Join-Path $root "pr132.patch"
+[System.IO.File]::WriteAllText($patchPath, $patchText, (New-Object System.Text.UTF8Encoding($false)))
+
+Write-Output "=== apply candidate fix ==="
+& git apply --check $patchPath
+if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
+    Write-Error "git apply --check failed: $LASTEXITCODE"
+    exit 21
+}
+& git apply $patchPath
+if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
+    Write-Error "git apply failed: $LASTEXITCODE"
+    exit 22
+}
+& gofmt -w internal/sem/provider.go internal/sem/provider_gitdir_unc_windows_test.go
+
+Write-Output "=== fixed focused test ==="
+$focusedLog = Join-Path $root "focused.log"
+& cmd.exe /d /c "$focused > `"$focusedLog`" 2>&1"
+$focusedExit = $LASTEXITCODE
+Get-Content $focusedLog
+Write-Output "FOCUSED_EXIT=$focusedExit"
+if ($focusedExit -ne 0) {
+    exit $focusedExit
+}
+
+Write-Output "=== full test suite ==="
+$fullLog = Join-Path $root "full.log"
+& cmd.exe /d /c "go test ./... > `"$fullLog`" 2>&1"
+$fullExit = $LASTEXITCODE
+Get-Content $fullLog
+Write-Output "FULL_EXIT=$fullExit"
+exit $fullExit
*** End Patch";
const result = await tools.apply_patch(patch);
text(result);

Root cause: the PR’s physical-path resolver handoff happens after an earlier bare-repository probe. For a repository entered through `SUBST`:

2. `resolver.lstat(dir\HEAD)` opens the parent and canonicalizes it to the backing path, e.g. `C:\...\checkout\subdir`.
